edits.proposed: One record per pensioner, identified with the recipient's own document (a survivor or substitute pension in the name of the person who receives it). Numeral 21 (element peju) carries the pension payments of the year - the monthly mesadas and the additional mesadas; numeral 23 (element apos) the health contribution deducted from the pension; numeral 24 (element apof) a solidarity-fund deduction where it applies; numeral 17 (element potro) any payment to the pensioner that is not the pension itself (e.g. a health-plan offset compensation); numeral 29 the withholding actually practised, which is nil where the pension does not exceed 1,000 UVT a month (ET art. 206 num. 5). Res. 227 art. 1.3.7.1.1 numerals 17, 21, 23, 24 and 29.

edits.current: Work-income payments with no dedicated numeral (Anexo T3.45 of Res. 000227/2025, element potro): non-habitual, one-off bonuses (a habitual bonus goes to numeral 5, element pasa), non-salary allowances, payments in kind that are not salary - including payments to third parties for the employee's benefit - (a payment in kind that constitutes salary goes to numeral 5, element pasa; the salary attribute of each in-kind wage type comes from the Wage Type Catalogue (WTC)), equity-based compensation, termination indemnities, and one-off payments to a retiree that are not a pension - a retirement gratuity, a pension-related compensation or settlement - while the pension itself goes to numeral 21 (element peju). Fed by the wage-type-to-numeral classification. Exclude advances, loans, expense reimbursements and other entries that are not income of the beneficiary. Informative wage types paid to third parties (the 'Inf.' wage types) and foreign-paid wage types are classified wage type by wage type on the same attributes: a wage type that is income of the beneficiary is reported in numeral 5 where it carries the salary attribute and here where it does not, whatever the payment channel; a wage type that records no income of the beneficiary (e.g. a reimbursement or an employer-cost informative entry) is excluded; a meal payment to a food supplier follows the numeral 7 / 8 / 32 rule; and the income of a non-resident for work performed entirely outside Colombia is foreign-source and is not reported in this return (DIAN Official letter 28380 of 2019). Accumulated on the payment date for the calendar tax year. Note the interaction with par. 6: numeral 7 must not repeat anything reported here.

Numeral 17 is the residual numeral: it carries every work-income payment not reported in a dedicated attribute, the counterpart of Form 220 casilla 46, whether one-off or recurring. Fed by the wage-type-to-numeral classification. Exclude advances, loans, expense reimbursements and other entries that are not income of the beneficiary. Informative wage types paid to third parties (the 'Inf.' wage types) and foreign-paid wage types are classified wage type by wage type on the same attributes: a wage type that is income of the beneficiary is reported in numeral 5 where it carries the salary attribute and here where it does not, whatever the payment channel; a wage type that records no income of the beneficiary (e.g. a reimbursement or an employer-cost informative entry) is excluded; a meal payment to a food supplier follows the numeral 7 / 8 / 32 rule; and the income of a non-resident for work performed entirely outside Colombia is foreign-source and is not reported in this return (DIAN Official letter 28380 of 2019). Accumulated on the payment date for the calendar tax year. Note the interaction with par. 6: numeral 7 must not repeat anything reported here.

edits.current: Pension income paid BY THE EMPLOYER (retirement, old-age or invalidity). Populated for every employer-paid pensioner: where the employer pays company pensions directly through payroll (monthly pension and additional pension wage types), this numeral is populated and the pensioner population, which is not part of the active employee master data, is included in the file. Fed by the pension wage types in the wage-type-to-numeral classification. Only the pension itself - the periodic retirement, old-age or invalidity pension payments - is reported here (Anexo T3.45 of Res. 000227/2025, element peju); a lump-sum or one-off payment to a retiree that is not a pension (a retirement gratuity, a pension-related compensation or settlement) is reported in numeral 17 (element potro). A survivor or substitute pension paid by the employer is reported in the record of the person who receives it, identified in numeral 2 with the recipient's own document type and number - not in a record of the deceased pensioner - the same identity rule as Form 220 casilla 50, issued in the recipient's name. Taxable only above 1,000 UVT per month (COP 52,374,000 in 2026) under ET art. 206 num. 5. Where a fund pays the pension, the fund is the withholding agent and reporting party and nothing is reported here.
